references.text: Moses had previously made the same demand that the sons of Gad and Reuben must cross the Jordan armed before the Lord before they can receive the land of Gilead as their possession.
The sons of Gad and Reuben confirm that they will cross the Jordan armed before the Lord, as Moses requires in verse 29.
Moses repeats the command that the armed men from Gad and Reuben must cross the Jordan ahead of their brothers until the land is conquered.
Joshua reminds the tribes of Reuben, Gad, and half-tribe of Manasseh of the agreement Moses made with them to cross the Jordan armed to help the other tribes.
Fulfillment of the promise: The sons of Reuben, Gad, and half-tribe of Manasseh cross the Jordan armed before the people of Israel, as Moses had commanded.
Joshua declares that the tribes of Reuben, Gad, and Manasseh have kept their promise and may return to their inherited land in Gilead.
Background for the conversation: The sons of Gad and Reuben asked to receive Gilead as their possession because the land was good for livestock.
